messages:
alicia-ae: Heads-up — Sasha from Borealis on the POC call. They ramped to ~60 RPS and are seeing slow first-token (TTFT) + intermittent 429s. request_id=abc123. Can eng/sre swarm?

sasha-borealis: repro notes: spike from 10->60 RPS, model=redwood/fast-7b, median first-token ~1800ms, tail 2.5s. 429s every ~30s. payloads ~120-300 tokens. no KV cache configured on client.

sam-eng: thanks. can you paste the 429 response headers / body and the client concurrency config? also are you using preflight/warmup calls?

sasha-borealis: here's one 429 (copied):

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: abc123
Retry-After: 2
{ "error": { "type": "rate_limit", "message": "capacity_throttle" }}

client: axios pool, concurrency=80, no client-side rate limiter. single region eu-west.

jon-sre: looks like gateway-level capacity_throttle. concurrency=80 is high for a single session without preflight. our soft burst per-tenant defaults to ~50 RPS for hosted. when you spike above that gateway starts returning 429s.

mira-ml: also flagging prompt behavior: no KV/prefix caching + long prompts -> model has to process many tokens for each request, increasing token compute per request and effective throughput needs. that can spike internal occupancy and surface throttle + higher TTFT.

sam-eng: quick triage checklist: reduce client concurrency to ~20, enable prefix_kv_cache or prefetch warmup, or request a temporary burst increase. for latency specifically reduce batch_window_ms to 10ms or set max_batch_size=8 for this tenant to favor TTFT over throughput.

alicia-ae: how painful would dedicated be for them? they'll ask about pricing if we recommend bumping commit.

jon-sre: rough: hosted with burst increase is fastest to unblock. Dedicated baseline for this workload (predictable 60 RPS sustained) usually needs a small reserved pool — I'll DM exact numbers to you, but it avoids gateway tenant-level throttles entirely.

sam-eng: sample client/route changes we can recommend to Borealis:

1) client: add a small warmup preflight request per worker on start:
```
POST /v1/generate
{ "model": "redwood/fast-7b", "input": "<short warmup prompt>", "warmup": true }
```
2) enable prefix KV cache in SDK: prefix_kv_cache: true
3) reduce concurrency and add token-aware rate limiter (e.g., 20 concurrent requests)
4) override batching: {"batch_window_ms": 10, "max_batch_size": 8} on their route config

mira-ml: also consider using the quant-variant (fast-7b-quant) as a fallback in routing policy (lower latency, slightly different quality). we can set prefer_warm_routing so traffic falls back automatically during throttles.

alicia-ae: jon, can we do a temporary soft-burst bump for borealis-tenant? they'll want to demo sustained load in 1hr.

jon-sre: granted a temporary soft-burst bump to 80 for tenant=borealis-tenant for 2 hours. applied routing tweak for prefer_warm_routing as canary.

deploy-bot: route: update applied -> tenant=borealis-tenant, soft_burst=80, prefer_warm_routing=true (deploy id: dpl-99821) :white_check_mark:

sasha-borealis: re-ran the test after changes — first-token now ~380ms median, tail ~700ms. no 429s in the last 3 minutes. big difference, thanks! :tada:

alicia-ae: great — i'll capture this before the exec demo. next steps: schedule follow-up w/ pricing + security checklist (KMS, VPC options). link to pricing doc: https://internal.redwood/pricing/dedicated-overview.

sam-eng: i'll follow up with a short runbook for their engineers: recommended client config + example SDK flags.

mira-ml: i'll create an eval to compare quality between fast-7b and fast-7b-quant on their prompt set so we can advise on fallback.

alicia-ae: awesome. closing the swarm, will circle back with quote + sec answers. :pray:
